 COMMON JUDGMENT  The petitioners have filed these two cases U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against the respondents seeking compensation for the injuries sustained by them in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. Since these two cases are arising out of one and same accident and cause of action are the same and the respondents are the same and to avoid multiplicity of proceedings and to avoid outcome of conflicting Judgments, these two cases are clubbed together.
M.V.C.No.2882/2023 clubbed with original M.V.C.No.2881/2023
and common evidence came to be recorded in the said case.
These two cases are proceeded for disposal by way of common Judgment.
03. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:

That on 16.02.2023 at about 02.45 p.m, the petitioner in M.V.C.No.2881/2023 was riding his Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-08-Q-4101 along with his wife and his minor children i.e., petitioner M.V.C.No.2882/2023 were going towards Malur from his native village Hedigenabele for getting treatment to his minor son at Malur hospital.

On the way when they reached in front of Vishwanatha Convention Hall on Hosakote - Malur Road, at that time, the Tipper Lorry bearing No.KA-53-AA-0252 came from Hosakote side towards Malur side, the driver of the said tipper lorry  (SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2881/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.2882/2023 Gruhith Kanchan vs Skanda Civicon Pvt Ltd on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120729139/
2 drove the same at a high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of which, the driver of the tipper lorry lost control over the vehicle and dashed his tipper lorry against the petitioner's Motor Cycle, due to which, both petitioners sustained grievous injuries.

24. Issue No.2 in M.V.C.No.2882/2023:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the minor petitioner in Road Traffic Accident.

The mother and natural guardian of the petitioner in her evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident the petitioner was aged about 08 years and was student studying in 2nd standard and she has incurred Rs.3,00,000/- towards medical treatment, attendant expenses, nutritious food etc.,.
Due to accidental injuries, the petitioner is unable to concentrate on his studies and suffering from permanent disability.

According to the evidence of PW.4, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that petitioner sustained degloving injury of left foot,
fracture talus left foot and he assessed total disability of left lower limb at 31% and that of his whole body at 16% of whole body and he has produced OPD card and X-ray film as per Ex.P.30 and 31.

26. It is admitted fact that the minor petitioner was travelling in the Motor Cycle of his father, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of Tipper Lorry,
he met with accident and sustained grievous injuries.
It is also admitted fact that the petitioner is a minor as on the date of accident.

It is admitted fact that he is a non-earning member of the family and he has no income and avocation and there is no evidence on  (SCCH-3) 21 M.V.C.No.2881/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.2882/2023 record to show that petitioner sustained any amputation or any loss of academic year.

27 . In this regard this tribunal has to consider the ratio laid down in Civil Appeal No.7139/2013 in a case of Master Mallikarjun V/s Divisional Manager, The National Insurance Co. Ltd., and another wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has held that,
 "Though it is difficult to have an accurate assessment of the compensation in the case of children suffering disability on account of a motor vehicle accident, having regard to the relevant factors,
precedents and the approach of various High Courts,
we are of the view that the appropriate compensation on all other heads in addition to the actual expenditure for treatment, attendant, etc., should be, if the disability is above 10% and upto 30% to the whole body, Rs.3,00,000; upto 60%, Rs.4,00,000; upto 90%,
Rs.5,00,000 and above 90%, it should be Rs.6,00,000.
For permanent disability upto 10%, it should be Rs.1,00,000, unless there are exceptional circumstances to take different yardstick.
 (SCCH-3) 22 M.V.C.No.2881/2023  c/w M.V.C.No.2882/2023  28.
